public_rationale: The paper version released June 2, 2026 reports five runs per task across 15 models and two benchmarks [e1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.16666v3). It finds that agents able to solve a task often fail to solve it consistently, supporting the claim that successful performance does not ensure success on every attempt [e1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.16666v3). Microsoft Research's May 15, 2026 discussion limits broader conclusions: its separate artifact-integrity stress test did not measure task completion or user satisfaction and was not representative of optimized production systems [e2](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/further-notes-on-our-recent-research-on-ai-delegation-and-long-horizon-reliability).
limitations: The June paper version was released within April–June 2026, but exact experiment dates are not separately reported.
The evaluations do not cover every model or workflow or establish that every narrow task must fail.
The findings do not establish a lack of practical usefulness or show that verification, oversight and specialized workflows cannot improve reliability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs cannot be trusted to do things right every time, even on tasks they mostly get right.

statement.excerpt: LLMs are sold as some sort of magic tool that can fix “anything” without ever specifying what that thing might be, mostly because they cannot be trusted, even in things that they mostly get right, to do things right every time.

our_interpretation: Assess the normalized reliability claim, not the surrounding claims about marketing or its motives.
The plain reading is that usually successful LLM workflows still produce occasional errors. It does not mean that every conceivable narrow task must fail.
For this ongoing observation, use the latest complete calendar quarter before publication: April through June 2026. Zitron supplied no reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: Repeated evaluations show that LLMs sometimes fail tasks they can ordinarily complete successfully.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative repeated evaluations establish dependable, error-free performance across the workflows covered by the claim. An isolated perfect benchmark score is insufficient.
